stage_a.note: Delivers a deeply emotional story about his parents, showing clear, positive, and meaningful engagement with the venture.
Highly animated and visibly excited when describing how his drops sell out in minutes.
Shows strong care and approachability when talking about taking care of his family and not being a burden.

venture.description: Customized rings made from spoons and other materials, sold via online drops driven by social media hype to Gen Z consumers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen introduces himself, asks for his investment, explains the concept of making rings from spoons, and describes his drop model.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: The panel opens their customized boxes, pours water to create a smoke effect, and handles the rings.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen shares the emotional origin story of starting the business after his father's heart attack and mother's cancer diagnosis.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks how long ago Tristen started this.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen states it was in 2017 and details his first sale of 155 rings from thrift store spoons.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks how many Instagram followers Tristen has.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen answers that he has 70,000 followers.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks about his presence on other platforms.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen says he just started on TikTok and has 15,000 followers there.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks what his overall sales are to date.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen reveals that his overall sales are $2.1 million.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks what his year-to-date sales are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen answers that year-to-date sales are $575,000.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark clarifies for the panel that a drop is a one-time sale where inventory is gone once sold out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen confirms that once they are gone, they are absolutely gone.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks how often he conducts his drops.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen states he does drops once a month right now.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks if he sells anything outside of the drops.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen answers no.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks for the average price of a ring.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen says the average price is $50.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks how many pieces were in the last drop and what the revenue was.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen says he sold 3,200 units for $155,000 in revenue.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks how quickly the rings sell out during a drop.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen explains the last one took about 24 hours, but some have sold out in 20 minutes.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin points out Tristen is a one-man band and asks what happens to his investment if Tristen gets hit by a bus.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen jokes that Kevin would be out of money and he would feel sorry for him.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin reiterates that this single point of failure is a real problem.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen admits it is a lean team but emphasizes his resourcefulness and work ethic to overcome challenges.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks how Tristen plans to scale the business and grow beyond the drop model.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen explains he wants to create a core collection to capture sales between drops and expand the brand.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks how old he was when he started.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen says he was 19, fresh out of high school, and is now 22.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori praises the business model but feels it is not an investable business for her, so she exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen accepts Lori's exit and asserts his desire to take the business as far as he can.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond explains it would take too much equity to make it worth his while and exits to avoid insulting him.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen shares his previous year's sales of $720k and strong 60% net margins to show the business's strength.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin offers $250k for 50%, requiring key man insurance, citing the risk of Tristen being a solo operator.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen pushes back on the risk, explaining he has people he can work with if needed.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark feels Tristen hasn't clearly communicated how to scale the business to $10 million and drops out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen notes he is projecting $1.6 million in sales this year just on drops to defend his valuation.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks if Tristen is ready to give up 50% for his projected sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen firmly answers no.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin urges Tristen to think about the value he brings to the table.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen insists that 50% equity is too much to give up.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara jumps in and offers $250k for 20% equity.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin immediately revises his offer down to $250k for 15% to undercut Barbara.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen asks Kevin why he drastically lowered his equity requirement.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin explains he feels a real connection and views it as a patron and young artist dynamic.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori jokes that Tristen is now in a funding frenzy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen clarifies the two standing offers from Barbara and Kevin.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara withdraws her offer and exits, stating she doesn't see his path to scale.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen acknowledges Barbara's exit and turns his attention back to Kevin's 15% offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara jokingly calls Kevin a bastard for undercutting her offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin celebrates undercutting Barbara and jokes about buying her a new broom.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin questions why Tristen would hesitate on a 15% deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen argues that 5% equity won't change Kevin's life and tries to negotiate further.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks Tristen directly what he wants to do.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Tristen accepts Kevin's offer.

decisions.note: Exits because she feels the business model is not investable for her.
Exits because he would require too much equity and doesn't want to insult the founder.

decisions.terms: $250,000 for 50% equity, with key man insurance.
decisions.note: Offers to solve the single point of failure problem by taking a large stake and requiring key man insurance.
Exits because the founder hasn't communicated a clear path to scale the business significantly.
Offers a deal at a lower equity stake than Kevin's.
Revises his offer down significantly to undercut Barbara's competing offer.
Withdraws her offer and exits because she fundamentally does not see his path to scale.

record.notes: The founder is highly emotional and engaging. S3 withdraws her offer and exits in the same turn.
